back: $P=|X|^2$; log-spectrogram $\log(P+\varepsilon)$ (or $10\log_{10}$ for dB) compresses dynamic range.
$m=2595\log_{10}(1+f/700)$, $f=700(10^{m/2595}-1)$; about linear below 1 kHz, logarithmic above.

front: Why does the mel scale exist?
back: Hearing resolves pitch roughly on a log scale: equal frequency ratios, not equal differences, sound like equal steps.

front: How is a mel filterbank built?
back: $M+2$ points equally spaced in mel, converted to Hz; filter $j$ is a triangle from $f_{j-1}$ up to $f_j$ and down to $f_{j+1}$, sampled at the FFT bin frequencies.

front: Shape of the filterbank matrix and how it is applied
back: $\mathbf H\in\mathbb R^{M\times(N/2+1)}$; mel spectrogram $=\mathbf P\mathbf H^\top\in\mathbb R^{T\times M}$ (one matmul).
80 log-mel bins, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop (Whisper-style); classifiers often use 64-128 mels.
Different window, mel variant (HTK/Slaney), filter normalisation, log base or `n_mels` between training and inference fails silently.
Window+FFT, power spectrum, mel filterbank, log, DCT; keep the first ~13 coefficients.

front: What does truncating the DCT keep?
back: The smooth spectral envelope (vocal-tract shape); it discards fast ripples such as pitch harmonics.

front: Why a DCT rather than a DFT here?
back: It is the DFT of a mirrored signal, so no wrap-around jump; real-valued and good energy compaction.
$\Delta c_t=\sum_{n=1}^N n(c_{t+n}-c_{t-n})/(2\sum_{n=1}^N n^2)$: least-squares slope over $2N+1$ frames.
The DCT's constant coefficient: overall log-energy level of the frame, often dropped or modelled separately.
